description: Finding 9, as Zig does it: streaming a short value needs the slot's position, which a sorted key can come without, so a two-byte key raises ExpectedSlotPosition while a long one works. There are three ways: the key reached by sorted_map_get with key; and a set's key-only entry reached by sorted_map_get with kv_pair in a read path, which leaves the entry where it is and gives it no position, so the key read_key_value_pair gives for it has none either. That is what getKeyValuePair does on a sorted map made over the set, read-only, or writable, where the map's init retags the set as a map first. Since 71ee0cf a key-only entry's key from read_key_value_pair has the entry's position when the entry has one, so a set's entry from an iterator streams in both (stream-short-set-key).
